newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea arrests ex-minister over arms scandal.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea arrests ex-minister over arms scandal.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors arrested sacked defence minister Lee Yang-ho, an executive of a leading local company and two employees of an arms dealer on Saturday in connection with an arms scandal, prosecution officials said.
"Mr Lee has been arrested and is taken to a Seoul prison," a prosecution official told Reuters. The others were also held.
Witnesses said two investigators led Lee, dressed in a dark suit, to a black limousine which whisked him off to the prison.

State prosecutors charged Lee, who was removed from President Kim Young-sam's cabinet last week, with bribery and leaking official secrets to the arms dealer, Kwon Pyong-ho, over a government purchase of military helicopters.
"Former minister Lee persistently denied bribery charges," senior prosecutor Ahn Kang-min told reporters.
"But he later admitted taking the money after investigators focused on the fact that he faced (an) extortion threat over bribery" by the employees of the arms dealer, Ahn said, without elaborating.

Among those arrested on Saturday were Lee Nam-hee and Kang Jong-ho, employees of a company owned by the arms dealer. The employees were charged by prosecutors with extorting 50 million won from former minister Lee by threatening to expose kickbacks.

The main opposition National Congress for New Politics has charged that Lee and the arms dealer split a 300 million won ($362,000) bribe from Daewoo Heavy Industries Ltd last year to arrange the government purchase.
Daewoo has denied the payment was a bribe.

Ex-minister Lee has not commented publicly on the charges, but state media earlier quoted him as denying any wrongdoing. Daewoo said it gave money to the arms dealer but insisted it was a commission, not a bribe.
Also arrested on Saturday was Sok Chin-chol, who was the president of Daewoo Heavy, a unit of Daewoo Group, last year. Sok now heads the group's car subsidiary in Poland.
The arms dealer, Kwon, had earlier told South Korean reporters in Beijing that he gave 150 million won to the ex-minister. Kwon's remarks were broadcast in South Korea.
Kwon is still believed to be in Beijing but could not be reached for comment.
The affair has embarrassed the president, who has staked his reputation on an anti-corruption drive that has led to the trial and conviction of ex-presidents Roh Tae-woo and Chun Doo Hwan.
Chun was sentenced to death and Roh to 22-1/2 years in jail after being found guilty in August of corruption, mutiny and treason. Both are appealing.

President Kim removed Lee from his post on October 17 as part of a reshuffle of the military's top brass. The reshuffle followed harsh criticism of the military for failing to prevent an incursion by a North Korean submarine last month.
Hours after Lee's dismissal, the National Congress accused Lee of taking the bribes, prompting the president to order a full investigation.
Lee headed the air force during Roh's presidency. He became defence minister after Kim succeeded Roh in 1993.
